protocol_notes: All PAC-NeRF numbers come from the official code (github.com/xuan-li/PAC-NeRF @ b613048), official per-scene configs; only data/output paths, n_cameras (3-view variant) and the Taichi memory pool fraction (0.6 -> 0.12/0.2, needed on shared GPUs) were changed.
rho is fixed to 1000 by the official configs (not optimised) and assumed 1000 by our model; GT = PAC-NeRF paper Table 1.
3-view variant uses the same canonical triplet t0 = cameras [4,6,7] as our model (docs/v3c/PACNERF_FEWSHOT.json), renumbered 0..2.

Engines differ: PAC-NeRF fits its own differentiable MPM to its own MPM renders (in-engine); our model was trained on a different simulator/action family and is applied zero-shot (K0) or with leave-one-scene-out offset calibration.
Wall-clock measured on shared A800-80GB GPUs (100% utilisation by other agents, up to 5 co-located v3g runs); treat as upper bounds; the README of PhysTwin and PAC-NeRF quote faster single-job times.
Errors: |log10 E_hat - log10 E_gt|, |nu_hat - nu_gt|, |log10 tauY_hat - log10 tauY_gt|.

notes.design: Hybrid = PAC-NeRF official dynamic stage (50+100 Adam iterations, official lr) started from the SAME static NeRF + initial-velocity checkpoints as the default run (<scene>_v11), with E, nu (and tauY) initialised from our model's calibrated prediction (bgsub, triplet t0, 3-seed ensemble, leave-one-scene-out offset; docs/v3g/pn_results/OURS.json) instead of the config defaults (torus E=1e5 nu=0.1; bird E=1e3 nu=0.1; playdoh E=1e5 nu=0.4 tauY=1e3; cat E=1e3 nu=0.2 tauY=1e2). Control = the default run's own dynamic stage (camera sampling RNG differs; a same-RNG default restart control torus_v11_rs was abandoned after 3 OOMs on the shared GPU).
notes.metrics: Loss is a single random camera per iteration and too noisy for a reach-the-same-loss criterion (both runs 'reach' the default's final smoothed loss at the first full-length iteration, 51). We therefore report reach-and-stay criteria on the parameter trajectory: first iteration after which log10 E stays within 0.05/0.1 of GT and of the default run's own final E (GT-free), and the same for tauY. Wall-clock per iteration differs between runs because of GPU sharing, so iteration counts are the comparable quantity.
notes.end_to_end_note: Under the official protocol the dynamic stage always runs a fixed 150 iterations and the static NeRF (6000 iterations) and velocity stages do not depend on the physical-parameter init, so end-to-end wall-clock is unchanged by a better init; savings would only materialise with early stopping.

protocol.data: Spring-Gaus mpm_synthetic (official Google Drive zip downloaded by v3f; 3 scenes extracted to data/external_datasets/v3g_springgaus_extract)
protocol.views: all 10 cameras used for training (official protocol); eval_cam 5 is one of the training cameras (render-only)
protocol.frames: first 20 of 30 frames (N_FRAME 20, dt 0.03 s) observed; frames 20-29 (0.60-0.87 s) are future prediction
protocol.stages: static 3DGS 30000 it -> velocity 100 it (+3000 Gaussian refine) -> dynamic spring-mass 300 it (+3000 refine first; n_step 100->150->200 at it 100/200) -> eval
protocol.metrics: Chamfer distance (mean of the two directed mean NN L2 distances, 8192-pt subsample, scene units; also squared x1e3) between Spring-Gaus anchor-interpolated Gaussian centres and GT MPM particles. Fit = frames 0-19 at training dt; future = frames 20-29 from its 60 Hz prediction rollout linearly interpolated in time; static baseline = GT frame 0 vs GT frame k. PSNR on eval cam 5 fit renders vs GT images. Metric code is ours (scripts/v3g/sg_eval.py): the official repo writes point clouds but ships no CD/EMD script, so numbers are not directly comparable to the paper table.
protocol.params: Spring-Gaus does not output E or nu: it learns per-anchor spring stiffness log10 k (2048 anchors, unit mass per anchor, init 3.0), friction, rebound, soft-k. Only the ranking of median log10 k vs GT E can be compared.
protocol.patches: build-compat only: #include <cfloat> added to submodules/simple-knn/simple_knn.cu (CUDA 12.6); env torch 2.4.1+cu121, pytorch3d 0.7.8, open3d 0.17.0, pillow 9.5.0 (pillow>=10 breaks its np.byte image loader); no algorithmic change
protocol.hardware: 1x NVIDIA A800-SXM4-80GB (GPU 7), shared with other jobs at ~100% util, so wall-clock is an upper bound
protocol.restart_note: torus was first started on GPU 0 at 01:30Z and aborted in the dynamic stage (GPU reassignment); restarted from scratch on GPU 7; the GPU-7 run is the one reported

ranking_check.note: GT E order torus(1e6) > duck(3e5) > apple(1e5). Spring-Gaus median log10 spring k 3.50 > 3.28 > 2.80: same order (3/3 pairs) although k is not convertible to Pa. Our K0 ensemble E/rho: duck 1.02e5 > torus 9.2e4 > apple 8.2e4 (2/3 pairs; torus-vs-duck wrong), all ~5-10x low; on the full 14-scene set (docs/v3f) our K0 E Spearman is -0.21, i.e. no ranking signal there.

phystwin_official.applicability_to_our_model: Not applicable: PhysTwin consumes multi-view RGB-D + hand-controller tracks of a real interaction and fits a per-scene spring-mass model (per-spring stiffness, no E/nu/sigma_y); there is no GT material parameter. Our feed-forward model takes rendered RGB video of a FieldBench-style loading and outputs continuum parameters. We report only cost (about 31 min of GPU optimisation per scene on a shared A800 vs. one forward pass for ours) and qualitative fit; no accuracy comparison is claimed.
